results.title: What Is NTP And PTP? - Asterfusion Data Technologies
results.content: One of the earliest standards for clock synchronization in networks was achieved through the utilization of the Network Time Protocol (NTP), which is based on Internet Protocol (IP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP). NTP serves to synchronize clocks between clients and servers, facilitating highly accurate time correction with a precision on the order of milliseconds. SNTP and NTP share the same format of network packets but differ in how the system handles their contents for time synchronization. PTP (Precision Time Protocol) is a time synchronization protocol used for high-precision frequency synchronization and phase synchronization between network nodes, with sub-microsecond time synchronization accuracy, which can meet the high-precision time synchronization requirements of radio and television networks, urban rail transit, wireless access networks and other scenarios. Precision Time Protocol (PTP) and Network Time Protocol (NTP) are often compared, and they differ in the following aspects:. Data centers require NTP/PTP synchronization to ensure time domain operation of the cluster. The Bank’s IT department utilizes data center clusters to operate in synchronized time domains that demand microsecond precision. The implementation of smart grid scenarios, such as relay protection and timely fault recovery in power networks, necessitates precise time synchronization among power devices to ensure swift fault recovery. Automation of industrial networks in order to ensure automated production, the requirements of the industrial terminals have a unified time, between the equipment to reach a high-precision time synchronization, the industry currently exists in two 1588v2 industrial network standards, IEEE 802.1AS and IEC 62439-3. PTP provides time synchronization services for industrial automation systems to ensure the coordination between machines, sensors, controllers and other devices. In scenarios where precise time measurement is required, such as radar, sonar, seismology, astronomy and other fields, PTP time synchronization technology can provide the required high-precision time reference. In intelligent transportation systems, PTP time synchronization is used to ensure precise time synchronization of traffic signals, vehicle monitoring and other traffic management systems, thereby improving traffic efficiency and safety. In security monitoring systems, PTP time synchronization ensures the time consistency of video recording, access control systems, and alarm systems, so that security incidents can be accurately traced and investigated.

Code Components extracted from this document must include Revised BSD License text as described in Section 4.e of the Trust Legal Provisions and are provided without warranty as described in the Revised BSD License.¶ * 2.PTP transport for NTP * 3.Network Correction Extension Field * 6.Implementation Status - RFC EDITOR: REMOVE BEFORE PUBLICATION The Precision Time Protocol (PTP) [IEEE1588] was designed for highly accurate synchronization of clocks in local networks. To avoid missing receive timestamps when the interface is receiving other traffic at a high rate, a filter is implemented in the hardware to inspect each received packet and capture a timestamp only for packets that need it.¶ The hardware filter can be usually configured for specific PTP transport (e.g. UDP over IPv4, UDP over IPv6, 802.3) and sometimes even the PTP message type (e.g. sync message or delay request) to further reduce the timestamping rate on the server or client side in the case of multicast messaging, but it typically cannot be configured to timestamp NTP messages sent to the UDP port 123.¶ Another issue for NTP is missing hardware support in network switches and routers. A server which is limited by the hardware timestamping rate cannot provide a highly accurate time service to the same number of clients as with PTP using multicast messaging.¶ ### Language The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119 [RFC2119].¶ 2.PTP transport for NTP A new TLV is defined for PTP to contain NTP messages in the client (3), server (4), and symmetric modes (1 and 2).

results.title: NTP, SNTP and PTP: what time synchronization do I need? | INCIBE-CERT | INCIBE
results.content: # NTP, SNTP and PTP: what time synchronization do I need? There are several synchronization mechanisms, the most common ones are the Simple Network Time Protocol (SNTP), Network Time Protocol (NTP) and Precision Time Protocol (PTP). The PTP protocol is the most accurate, in the nanosecond range, while the SNTP and NTP protocols are less accurate, in the microsecond range, but are sufficient for certain industrial and commercial needs. In both the NTP and SNTP protocols the communication begins with a request message by the client. The NTP protocol can use various servers and takes into account the tripping speed of the component that requests the time. As it uses several devices, the NTP method can distinguish the time of those that move away from the others. This gives the NTP protocol more reliability than SNTP, which only uses one server or master clock. Both protocols are interoperable, in other words, a device that operates with SNTP can connect to another that uses NTP and vice versa. * A first message is sent (synchronization request) at the T0 instant on the client’s side that checks if the time lag between the server and the requester is greater than 17 minutes. One advantage of this protocol is the ability to implement encryption between server and client for a secure connection in order to ensure the authenticity of the source. The use of the SNTP protocol as a main source or clock is not recommended. Unlike NTP and SNTP, in the PTP protocol the connection begins with a server request. The client's clock performs t2-t1 and adds it to the time in its own clock, obtaining the time corresponding to the server's time without taking the delay caused by the sending speed and internal requests into account. The time that the server takes to process the message packets is the same time that the client takes to do the same. Organizations should use servers with a GPS mechanism as a zero layer synchronization method and implement firewalls that prevent the entry of commands that can make time variations in case of the using of NTP and SNTP methods. If our devices do not need high accuracy, the use of NTP and SNTP protocols is appropriate.
